subject: Political Science (Code: 323)
past_paper_reference: CUET UG Political Science Past Papers (2022-2024)

questions.question: What was the official election symbol of the Indian National Congress during the first three general elections (1952, 1957, and 1962)?
options: A) Two bullocks with a yoke
questions.explanation: During the first three general elections, the Congress party's symbol was 'two bullocks with a yoke'. It later adopted 'cow and calf' in 1971 and the 'hand' in 1978.

questions.question: The landmark States Reorganisation Act, which established 14 states and 6 union territories on linguistic lines, officially came into effect on:
questions.explanation: The States Reorganisation Act was enacted by Parliament in 1956 and came into legal force on 1 November 1956.

questions.question: Which prestigious Indian statistical journal was founded in 1933 by Professor P.C. Mahalanobis, serving as a platform for economic planning theory?
questions.explanation: P.C. Mahalanobis founded 'Sankhya: The Indian Journal of Statistics' in 1933 at the Indian Statistical Institute.

questions.question: Which iconic slogan was coined by Prime Minister Lal Bahadur Shastri during the 1965 Indo-Pakistani war to inspire soldiers and boost food production?
questions.explanation: Lal Bahadur Shastri gave the slogan 'Jai Jawan, Jai Kisan' (Hail the Soldier, Hail the Farmer) in October 1965 to galvanize the nation.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Who was serving as the Vice-President and Acting President of India following the demise of Dr. Zakir Husain before resigning to contest the presidency in 1969?
questions.explanation: Varahagiri Venkata Giri (V.V. Giri) was Vice-President and took over as Acting President in May 1969, resigning in July 1969 to run as an independent candidate.

questions.question: In the sixth general elections of March 1977, how many Lok Sabha seats were won by the Janata Party on its own, securing an absolute majority?
questions.explanation: The Janata Party won 295 seats on its own (and 330 with its allies), securing a comfortable majority to form the first non-Congress Union government.

questions.question: In which year was the Memorandum of Settlement on Punjab (Rajiv Gandhi - Longowal Accord) signed in New Delhi?
questions.explanation: The Rajiv-Longowal Accord was signed on 24 July 1985 to resolve regional demands concerning Chandigarh, river water sharing, and rehabilitation.

questions.question: Which grassroots cooperative organisation founded in 1964 by Chandi Prasad Bhatt in Gopeshwar provided the organizational foundation for the Chipko movement?
questions.explanation: Chandi Prasad Bhatt founded the Dasholi Gram Swarajya Sangh (DGSS) in 1964, which organized local villagers to resist commercial forestry and started the Chipko protests in 1973.

questions.question: What percentage of jobs in Central Government civil services and public sector undertakings was reserved for Other Backward Classes under the Mandal Commission recommendations?
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission recommended a 27% quota for OBCs so that the total reservations for SC, ST, and OBC combined did not exceed 50%.

questions.question: In April 1999, the second coalition government led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee fell after losing a vote of confidence in the Lok Sabha by a margin of:
questions.explanation: The 13-month-old Vajpayee government lost the trust vote on 17 April 1999 by 269 votes to 270 (a margin of a single vote) after the AIADMK withdrew support.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The US foreign policy doctrine announced in March 1947 pledging financial and military support to nations resisting communist subversion was known as the:
questions.explanation: President Harry S. Truman articulated the Truman Doctrine in March 1947, providing aid to Greece and Turkey to prevent Soviet influence.

questions.question: In which year was Soviet leader Mikhail Gorbachev awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for his leading role in ending Cold War tensions and promoting democratic reforms?
questions.explanation: Mikhail Gorbachev received the Nobel Peace Prize in October 1990 for his peace initiatives and allowing democratic transitions in Eastern Europe.

questions.question: The global military reach of the United States is structurally organized through how many geographic Unified Combatant Commands encompassing the entire planet?
questions.explanation: The US Department of Defense assigns global operational responsibility across six geographic Unified Combatant Commands (e.g., USINDOPACOM, USEUCOM, USCENTCOM).

questions.question: In 2012, which regional integration organization was awarded the Nobel Peace Prize for advancing peace, reconciliation, democracy, and human rights across its continent?
questions.explanation: The European Union received the Nobel Peace Prize in 2012 for transforming Europe from a continent of war into a continent of peace over six decades.

questions.question: The permanent headquarters and central Secretariat of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) is located in:
questions.explanation: The ASEAN Secretariat was established in 1976 and is permanently situated in Jakarta, Indonesia.

questions.question: In which year did the Republic of Maldives amend its political system to officially introduce a multi-party democratic system?
questions.explanation: In June 2005, the Maldivian Parliament (Majlis) voted unanimously to legalize political parties, ending decades of one-party presidential rule.

questions.question: The international headquarters of the United Nations is situated in which city?
questions.explanation: The United Nations headquarters has been situated along the East River in New York City since 1951.

questions.question: The World Health Organization (WHO), the specialized UN agency responsible for international public health, is headquartered in:
questions.explanation: The WHO was founded on 7 April 1948 and is headquartered in Geneva, Switzerland.

questions.question: In traditional security analysis, an alliance is best understood as a coalition of sovereign states that coordinate their military policies to:
options: A) Abolish all national currencies across member countries
B) Conduct joint cultural literacy programmes in rural villages
C) Deter or defend against military aggression by adversary states
D) Transfer all police authority to international court judges
questions.explanation: Traditional military alliances (e.g. NATO, Warsaw Pact) are formed by sovereign states through mutual defense treaties to deter adversaries or defend against armed attacks.

questions.question: The historic 1992 Earth Summit held in Rio de Janeiro, Brazil, was unprecedented because it brought together representatives from more than:
questions.explanation: Over 170 sovereign states, thousands of NGOs, and multinational delegations participated in the 1992 Earth Summit (UNCED) in Rio de Janeiro.

questions.question: The World Social Forum (WSF), serving as an open meeting place for reflective thinking and democratic debate against neoliberalism, convenes its global assemblies:
questions.explanation: The WSF meets on an annual basis, bringing together social movements, trade unions, and grassroots activists to organize alternatives to corporate globalization.

questions.question: The princely state of Junagadh, which experienced accession tensions in 1947, was located on the southwestern peninsula of:
questions.explanation: Junagadh was a maritime princely state situated in the southwestern part of the Kathiawar/Saurashtra peninsula in present-day Gujarat.

questions.question: In the first general elections of 1952, which opposition party secured the second-largest share of the popular national vote (approximately 10.6%) after the Congress?
questions.explanation: The Socialist Party secured 10.6% of the national vote in 1952, though the first-past-the-post electoral system translated this into only 12 Lok Sabha seats.

questions.question: The High Yielding Variety (HYV) seed technology introduced during the Green Revolution required which critical combination of farm inputs to achieve high productivity?
options: A) Pure organic manure and complete absence of water canals
B) Dryland farming with zero chemical additions
C) Traditional wooden ploughs without tractor mechanisation
D) Reliable irrigation, chemical fertilizers, and pesticides
questions.explanation: HYV dwarf crop seeds could not produce high yields without a package of complementary inputs: assured water through canal/tube-well irrigation, chemical fertilizers, and plant protection pesticides.

questions.question: In December 1949, independent India demonstrated its independent foreign policy by becoming one of the very first non-communist nations to formally recognize:
options: A) The People's Republic of China (PRC)
C) The Republic of South Africa
questions.explanation: India recognized the newly established People's Republic of China on 30 December 1949, wishing to build warm relations with its Asian neighbor.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: Before serving as Congress President and head of the 'Syndicate', K. Kamaraj had gained immense national acclaim as the Chief Minister of:
questions.explanation: K. Kamaraj served as Chief Minister of Madras State from 1954 to 1963, pioneering the famous midday meal scheme in primary schools before proposing the 'Kamaraj Plan'.

questions.question: Before leading the student movements in 1974, Jayaprakash Narayan had retired from electoral party politics in the 1950s to dedicate himself to which Gandhian movement?
options: C) Bhoodan and Sarvodaya movement led by Acharya Vinoba Bhave
questions.explanation: JP withdrew from active party politics in 1954 to dedicate his life to Vinoba Bhave's Bhoodan (land gift) and Gramdan movements for peaceful social reconstruction.

questions.question: In 1939, Sheikh Abdullah renamed his political party from the 'All Jammu and Kashmir Muslim Conference' to which secular organization?
questions.explanation: Sheikh Abdullah secularized the movement in June 1939 by transforming the Muslim Conference into the National Conference, welcoming members of all religious communities.

questions.question: The Narmada River, where the Sardar Sarovar and other major dams were constructed, flows westward across which three Indian states before entering the sea?
options: A) Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, and Gujarat
C) Odisha, Chhattisgarh, and Andhra Pradesh
D) Karnataka, Kerala, and Tamil Nadu
questions.explanation: The Narmada originates at Amarkantak in Madhya Pradesh and flows westward through MP, Maharashtra, and Gujarat into the Gulf of Khambhat (Arabian Sea).

questions.question: The National Democratic Alliance (NDA), a coalition of non-Congress parties led by the Bharatiya Janata Party, was formally established in which year?
questions.explanation: The NDA was formed in May 1998 under the leadership of Atal Bihari Vajpayee and L.K. Advani to provide a stable national coalition government.

questions.question: Before undertaking his fatal hunger strike for an Andhra state, Potti Sreeramulu was renowned as a dedicated Gandhian who had undertaken earlier fasts in Madras to demand:
options: A) Immediate industrial nationalisation of private textile mills
B) The establishment of mandatory military conscription for college students
C) Temple entry and civic equality for Dalits (Harijans)
D) The banning of all english-language higher education institutions
questions.explanation: Potti Sreeramulu was a devoted Gandhian who fasted in Nellore and Madras in the late 1940s demanding that Hindu temples be opened to Dalits.

questions.question: According to political scientist W.H. Morris-Jones, India's one-party dominance under the Congress was distinct from single-party systems in other post-colonial states because:
options: A) It banned all opposition parties by presidential decree.
B) It functioned without a written constitution or independent courts.
C) It required all civil servants to be formal members of the ruling party.
D) It operated within a vibrant framework of competitive elections, constitutional civil liberties, and open political criticism.
questions.explanation: Morris-Jones argued that Congress dominance was unique because it existed within an open, competitive democratic system where opposition parties freely organized and criticized the government.

questions.question: The National Development Council (NDC), established in August 1952 to bridge Union and State developmental priorities, comprised:
options: A) The Prime Minister, Union Cabinet Ministers, Chief Ministers of all States, and Members of the Planning Commission
B) Exclusively the Governors of all States and the Chief Justice of India
C) Only the Union Finance Minister and the Reserve Bank of India Governor
D) The Presidents of all recognized national political parties
questions.explanation: The NDC brought together the executive heads of both the Union (PM, Cabinet, Planning Commission) and the States (all Chief Ministers) to review and approve national Five Year Plans.

questions.question: The historic 1955 Bandung Conference concluded with the unanimous adoption of a declaration containing how many principles for promoting world peace and cooperation?
questions.explanation: The Bandung Conference adopted the 'Ten Principles of Bandung' (Dasasila Bandung), elaborating on Panchsheel and incorporating the UN Charter's human rights principles.

questions.topic: Challenge to and Restoration of Congress System
questions.question: In the fourth general elections of 1967, the Congress party failed to secure an absolute majority in how many state legislative assemblies across the country?
options: A) In every single state assembly without exception
B) In only one state assembly
C) Seven state assemblies (and lost power in two others due to defections)
D) In all union territories exclusively
questions.explanation: In 1967, Congress was defeated in seven states (Punjab, Haryana, UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Orissa, Madras, and Kerala) and lost two more through post-poll defections, losing control over nine states.

questions.question: According to the official investigation of the Shah Commission of Inquiry, approximately how many individuals were detained across India under preventive detention laws during the Emergency?
questions.explanation: The Shah Commission documented that approximately 110,806 people were arrested under MISA, DISIR, and other preventive detention measures between June 1975 and March 1977.

questions.question: The armed secessionist movement in the Mizo Hills led by Laldenga was precipitated by the local population's anger over the Assam government's inadequate response to which famine in 1959?
options: A) Mautam Famine (caused by bamboo flowering and rat plagues)
questions.explanation: In 1959, the cyclical bamboo flowering (Mautam) caused a rat population explosion that devoured food crops. Inadequate famine relief from the Assam government led Laldenga to form the MNF in 1961.

questions.sub_topic: First Jan Sunwai Date and Place
questions.question: The Mazdoor Kisan Shakti Sangathan (MKSS) organized independent India's first historic 'Jan Sunwai' (public hearing) to expose corruption in local development works on 2 December 1994 at:
options: B) Kotkirana in Pali district, Rajasthan
questions.explanation: On 2 December 1994, MKSS held its first Jan Sunwai in Kotkirana, Rajasthan, reading out public expenditure records aloud before local villagers to audit panchayat accounts.

questions.question: Because post-independence Indian censuses (except 1931) did not enumerate caste populations other than SCs and STs, the Mandal Commission estimated the OBC population by extrapolating from:
options: C) The 1931 Census of British India
questions.explanation: The Mandal Commission used caste data from the 1931 census (the last comprehensive caste census) to estimate that OBCs accounted for 52% of the Indian population.

questions.topic: Cold War Era and Non-aligned Movement
questions.question: The European Recovery Program, famously known as the Marshall Plan (1948-1952), disbursed over $13 billion in US economic aid primarily to:
options: A) Finance the industrial reconstruction of the Soviet Union and Eastern Europe
B) Construct nuclear submarine bases across Latin America
C) Provide food aid exclusively to newly decolonized African states
D) Rebuild war-devastated Western European economies and prevent the electoral spread of communism
questions.explanation: Named after Secretary of State George Marshall, the plan revived Western Europe's industrial capacity, integrated trade, and diminished the political appeal of communist parties.

questions.question: The three Baltic republics (Estonia, Latvia, and Lithuania), which were the first to break away from the Soviet Union, consolidated their integration with the West in 2004 by joining:
options: A) Both NATO and the European Union
B) The Commonwealth of Independent States (CIS)
D) The Warsaw Pact Economic Council
questions.explanation: In spring 2004, all three Baltic states formally acceded to both the North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) and the European Union (EU).

questions.question: Which of the following statesmen was the Foreign Minister of Singapore who signed the Bangkok Declaration in 1967, establishing ASEAN?
questions.explanation: Sinnamamby Rajaratnam represented Singapore as its Foreign Minister and was one of the five founding signatories of the Bangkok Declaration in August 1967.

questions.question: In April 1984, the Indian Army launched 'Operation Meghdoot' to preempt Pakistani military occupation and gain control of the highest battlefield in the world at the:
options: C) Siachen Glacier in the Karakoram range
questions.explanation: Operation Meghdoot was launched on 13 April 1984, successfully securing the Siachen Glacier and its key mountain passes before Pakistan could deploy troops.

questions.question: Unlike specialized agencies that report primarily to ECOSOC, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) reports directly to:
options: A) The International Court of Justice exclusively
B) The World Trade Organization Ministerial Council
D) Both the UN General Assembly and the UN Security Council
questions.explanation: Given the critical link between nuclear technology, non-proliferation, and international peace, the IAEA reports annually to the General Assembly and directly to the Security Council when non-compliance is detected.

questions.question: Non-traditional security concepts differ fundamentally from traditional security approaches because their primary referent object of security is:
options: A) The individual human being and communities (Human Security), rather than merely the state and its borders
B) The territorial borders of naval superpowers exclusively
C) The preservation of interstate military alliances
D) The commercial profits of multinational defense contractors
questions.explanation: Non-traditional security moves beyond state-centric defense to prioritize 'Human Security', protecting individuals and peoples from threats like hunger, disease, environmental disasters, and terrorism.

questions.question: The Linguistic Provinces Commission (Dhar Commission) appointed by Constituent Assembly President Dr. Rajendra Prasad in June 1948 concluded in its report that:
options: A) India should be divided into 500 micro-linguistic autonomous principalities within six months.
B) The formation of provinces purely on linguistic considerations was not in the larger interests of the Indian nation, and administrative convenience should be the primary criterion.
C) Language should be the sole, mandatory basis for all internal state boundaries without exception.
D) All linguistic states should maintain separate independent armies and national passports.
questions.explanation: The Dhar Commission (Dec 1948) cautioned that linguistic states could threaten national integration, recommending that states be reorganized on administrative, financial, and geographical considerations.

questions.question: In the draft plan-frame for the Second Five Year Plan, Professor P.C. Mahalanobis argued that priority development of heavy machine-building industries was essential because:
options: A) It would eliminate the need for any agricultural production or irrigation canals.
B) It would allow India to export 100% of its heavy steel production exclusively to the United States.
C) It would build domestic capital goods capacity, freeing India from structural import dependency on advanced industrial economies for capital goods.
D) It was mandated as a formal condition for membership in the United Nations Security Council.
questions.explanation: Mahalanobis recognized that depending on foreign machines to produce consumer goods created long-term balance-of-payments vulnerability, making domestic heavy industry the cornerstone of economic independence.

questions.question: The six-nation Colombo Conference proposals of December 1962 sought to create conditions for Sino-Indian peace by suggesting that in the Western sector (Ladakh):
options: A) India should formally surrender the entire state of Jammu and Kashmir to China.
B) China should dismantle all military garrisons in Tibet and transfer Tibet to UN trusteeship.
C) Both countries should permanently merge their armed forces into an Afro-Asian joint command.
D) Chinese military forces should withdraw 20 kilometres behind their line of actual control, while the evacuated area would become a demilitarized zone administered by civilian posts.
questions.explanation: The Colombo Proposals suggested a 20-km Chinese withdrawal in the western sector creating a demilitarized buffer zone with civilian posts, a compromise India accepted in principle but China rejected.

questions.question: To correct the judicial abnegation witnessed during the Emergency in the ADM Jabalpur case, the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act (1978) amended Article 359 to provide that:
options: A) The right to move courts for the enforcement of fundamental rights under Articles 20 and 21 can never be suspended, even during a proclamation of National Emergency.
B) The Supreme Court of India could never hear any constitutional petition during peacetime.
C) The President could suspend all fundamental rights without issuing any gazette notification.
D) All preventive detention laws were permanently declared unconstitutional across India.
questions.explanation: The 44th Amendment barred the suspension of Articles 20 (protection against retrospective criminal laws) and 21 (right to life and personal liberty) even during an Emergency, preventing future repetitions of ADM Jabalpur.

questions.question: The 1992 Maastricht Treaty structured the European Union upon 'Three Pillars'. Which of the following accurately identifies these three pillars?
options: A) Pillar 1: NATO Alliance; Pillar 2: Warsaw Pact; Pillar 3: Non-Aligned Secretariat
B) Pillar 1: European Communities (EC, ECSC, Euratom); Pillar 2: Common Foreign and Security Policy (CFSP); Pillar 3: Justice and Home Affairs (JHA / PJCCM)
C) Pillar 1: Agricultural Subsidies; Pillar 2: Space Exploration; Pillar 3: Maritime Piracy
D) Pillar 1: Western European Union; Pillar 2: League of Nations; Pillar 3: Bretton Woods
questions.explanation: The Maastricht Treaty established the three-pillar architecture: supranational European Communities (Pillar 1), intergovernmental CFSP (Pillar 2), and police/judicial cooperation in criminal matters (Pillar 3), lasting until the 2009 Lisbon Treaty consolidated them.
